extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for processing requests for continued examination (RCEs) under 37 CFR 1.114 and transitional after-final submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a), including eligibility, submission content, processing steps, and consequences of improper or nonresponsive filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new matter for amendments filed with 37 CFR 1.17(r) / 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of 35 U.S.C. 132, no amendment considered as a result of payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) (or entered pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114) may introduce new matter into the disclosure of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission may comprise an IDS, an amendment to the written description, claims or drawings, new substantive argument and/or new evidence, but any amendment determined to contain new matter should be treated as a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 that contains new matter (see MPEP § 706.03(o)). If applicant seeks to add new matter, the procedure in 37 CFR 1.114 is not available and the applicant must file a continuation-in-part under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Also, an RCE cannot be used to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from previously claimed and examined claims (i.e., cannot switch inventions; see 37 CFR 1.145).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for transitional procedure under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application qualifies under 37 CFR 1.129(a) if it was filed on or before June 8, 1995 and has an effective U.S. filing date of June 8, 1993 or earlier (and other statutory/pending requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must check whether the submission and the 37 CFR 1.17(r) fee were filed prior to the filing of the Appeal Brief and prior to abandonment. The form paragraph may apply only in applications (utility/plant) filed prior to June 9, 1995 which have been pending for at least two years as of June 8, 1995 (taking into account 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c)) and where no previous 1.17(r) fee has been paid. If a Notice of Appeal and appeal fee were filed prior to or with payment of the 1.17(r) fee, payment is construed as a request to dismiss the appeal and continue prosecution under 1.129(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of timely payment of 37 CFR 1.17(r) fee (transitional) or 37 CFR 1.17(e) fee (RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the timely payment of the applicable fee, the finality of the previous Office action is withdrawn and previously unentered submissions (and those filed with the fee) will be entered and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment was timely filed in reply to a final rejection but the fee did not accompany it, examiners will continue expedited consideration per MPEP § 714.13 and issue an advisory action notifying applicant whether the amendment has been entered. If an advisory action indicated non-entry, applicant may later pay the fee to obtain entry. A conditional payment (authorization to charge deposit account or credit card) is treated as an unconditional payment. Absent specific instructions, conflicting amendments are entered in order filed; applicants should clarify which amendments to enter when conflicts exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and sufficiency of 'submission' under 37 CFR 1.114/1.129
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement (IDS), an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111. An appeal brief or reply brief (or related papers) is not a submission, although arguments from an appeal/reply brief may be incorporated by reference or resubmitted. Previously filed amendments after final (entered or not) may satisfy the submission requirement. Arguments entered after final that were not persuasive may nonetheless satisfy the submission requirement if they are responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 (eligibility and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request continued examination by filing a submission and paying the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) prior to the earliest of: payment of the issue fee (unless a petition under 1.313 is granted), abandonment, or filing a notice of appeal/commencing certain civil actions. Prosecution in the application must be closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.114 applies to utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or international applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. It does not apply to provisional applications, utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, international applications filed before June 8, 1995, design applications, or patents under reexamination. 'Prosecution closed' means the application is under appeal, or the last Office action is a final action, notice of allowance, or otherwise closes prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing checklist for RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support personnel must verify a set of conditions before processing an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify: (A) RCE filed on or after May 29, 2000; (B) application filed on or after June 8, 1995; (C) application is utility or plant (not design); (D) application was pending when RCE was filed (not patented or abandoned); (E) prosecution is closed (final rejection, notice of allowance, Quayle, or under appeal); (F) RCE filed before payment of issue fee or, if not, that petition under 1.313 to withdraw from issue was filed and granted; (G) RCE accompanied by proper fees including 1.17(e); (H) RCE included a submission as required by 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more conditions for filing an RCE are not satisfied, the applicant will be notified and the RCE will be treated as improper; it will not toll any running time in the prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally mail Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (Form PTO-2051). If prosecution is not closed, notify applicant and enter any amendment/reply and forward to examiner for consideration under 37 CFR 1.111. If the application is under appeal and the RCE lacks fee/submission, forward to examiner and notify applicant. If improper RCE forwarded in error to examiner, return application to head supervisory legal instruments examiner (HSLIE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous transmittal paper (CPA vs RCE) resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: If transmittal paper is ambiguous as to whether it requests a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) or an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114, and the application is eligible for either (plant/utility filed on/after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000), resolve ambiguity in favor of treating it as a CPA under 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References or other papers filed with the transmittal paper (e.g., preliminary amendment or IDS) will not be taken into account in determining whether the transmittal paper is a CPA or RCE. This rule applies only where the application is eligible for either practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of conditional RCE or conditional payment
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission accompanied by a 'conditional' RCE and payment authorization (authorization to charge deposit account) will be treated as if an RCE and payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e) had been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same treatment applies for conditional payments under transitional 1.129(a) (e.g., conditional authorization to charge 1.17(r) fee is treated as unconditional payment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and processing of amendments upon proper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If conditions for filing an RCE are satisfied, previously filed unentered submissions, amendments filed with the RCE, and amendments filed prior to the mailing of the next Office action will normally be entered and the application forwarded to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent specific instructions, all amendments filed as of the date the RCE is filed are entered in the order filed. Applicants are encouraged to file all amendments no later than the RCE filing to avoid disapproval of entry under 37 CFR 1.111(b). Consider filing a suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(c) with the RCE if additional time is needed for a supplement (e.g., affidavit/test data). RCE filers do not need to pay excess claims fees previously paid; new claims in excess of previously paid-for claims will require payment under 37 CFR 1.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA treated as RCE and petition to convert to 1.53(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CPA of a utility or plant application is filed on or after May 29, 2000 (to which CPA practice no longer applies), the Office will treat the improper CPA as an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the CPA does not satisfy 1.114 (e.g., lacks submission or fee), it is treated as an improper RCE and the time in the last Office action continues to run. If the applicant does not want the CPA treated as an RCE (e.g., divisional CPA), the applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) requesting conversion to an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b). The petition must include: (A) $130 fee; (B) true copy of the complete nonprovisional application as filed designated as the prior nonprovisional; (C) any amendments entered in the prior nonprovisional; (D) any amendments submitted but not entered directed to be entered in the application papers; (E) an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 if not already submitted. The Office will not grant such a petition unless it is before an appropriate deciding official before an Office action has been mailed in response to the RCE as treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of RCE filed after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant timely files an RCE with the fee and a submission after a final rejection, the Office will withdraw the finality of the Office action and the submission will be entered and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.114(d). If a reply to a final Office action is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111. Mere request for and payment of the RCE fee will not toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment—an adequate submission is required. Use form paragraph 7.42.04 to notify applicant that finality has been withdrawn; use 7.42.08 if the submission does not comply with 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive submission under RCE (bona fide attempt requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission filed under 37 CFR 1.114 in reply to a final Office action is not fully responsive, it must nonetheless be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply in order for the RCE to toll the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission appears bona fide, applicant must be informed why it is not fully responsive and given a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever is longer) from the mailing date of the notice to submit a complete reply (this supersedes the prior time period and may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a)); use form paragraph 7.42.08. If the submission is not a bona fide attempt (for example, an IDS alone when a reply is outstanding), the RCE should be treated as improper and a Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (PTO-2051) should be mailed; the RCE will not toll the period and the application may be abandoned if no compliant reply is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for making the first action final after filing under 37 CFR 1.129(a) or 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: The next Office action on the merits after a submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) or 37 CFR 1.114 may be made final only under the conditions for making a first action in a continuing application final set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate to make the first action final following a transitional submission or an RCE, use the corresponding form paragraphs (e.g., 7.42.03 for 1.129(a), 7.42.09 for 1.114) and remind applicant of extension of time policy under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Shortened statutory reply periods (three months, with further clarifications about replies filed within two months and advisory actions) apply as described in the form paragraphs.
